messages.content: Let’s do the hotel comparison now. I want one good historic-district choice and one genuinely cheaper option across the river. Make sure the room listing actually allows Daniel, Owen, and me, not just two adults. Four nights, Friday March 27 through Tuesday March 31.

I’ll compare the full four-night cost, room setup, cancellation terms, parking, and the practical trip into central Charleston. Are you planning to rent a car, or should I price the across-river option around rides and public transit?
No rental car at this point. We’ll use rides if we stay outside the center, but tell me whether the bus is realistic. Also include airport transportation so the hotel savings aren’t exaggerated.

I found two strong candidates with rooms explicitly listed for three guests. The central option is Hyatt House Charleston/Historic District: a king studio suite with a full-size sofa bed, maximum occupancy four. The current flexible rate is $1,276 for four nights, plus $178.64 in lodging taxes and fees, for $1,454.64. Valet parking is $49 nightly plus tax, but without a car that charge does not apply. Cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. local time on March 25; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. Breakfast is included.

The lower-cost option is Cambria Hotel Charleston Riverview: two queen beds, maximum occupancy four. The flexible room charge is $812, with $113.68 in taxes and fees, totaling $925.68. Surface parking is complimentary. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. local time on March 26, then one night plus tax. Breakfast is available but not included.
How central is the Hyatt House in practice? Historic District can mean a lot of things.

It is on upper King Street, near the visitor-center side of the district rather than the waterfront. Restaurants along upper King are generally a 3- to 10-minute walk. Marion Square is about 12 minutes on foot, City Market about 22 minutes, and Waterfront Park roughly 28 minutes. The free DASH shuttle can shorten some trips during operating hours. It is central enough to avoid routine rides, though it is not in the compact Market and waterfront core.
And the Cambria? Give me a realistic day, not just the mileage.

Cambria is west of the Ashley River. A ride to Marion Square is usually 10 to 15 minutes in light traffic and 18 to 25 minutes at busier periods. Typical one-way pricing is about $13 to $21 before tip, with surge pricing possible. If you go downtown once each morning and return after dinner, four days of round trips would likely cost $120 to $190 before tips. Returning to the hotel midday would add roughly $26 to $42 each time and erode the savings quickly.
What about the bus? Owen won’t care, but I don’t want to spend an hour each way.

The bus is possible but not efficient from that hotel. Reaching the nearest useful CARTA stop involves a walk, and most central trips require waiting plus either a transfer or a longer approach. Plan on about 40 to 55 minutes each way under a workable schedule, compared with roughly 15 to 25 minutes by ride. Evening frequency is the larger problem. I would treat the bus as an occasional fallback, not the main plan for a four-day family visit.
Add the airport legs. We land at 11:31 Friday and leave at 4:55 Tuesday.

From CHS to Hyatt House, allow about 20 to 30 minutes in the car after pickup and $28 to $40 before tip. Tuesday, leaving the hotel around 2:30 p.m., the ride should be about 20 to 25 minutes and another $28 to $40. Estimated airport rides total $56 to $80.

CHS to Cambria is usually 18 to 25 minutes and about $25 to $36. The Tuesday return is similar, so estimate $50 to $72 total. Cambria saves only about $6 to $8 on the airport pair; its meaningful transportation cost is the repeated downtown travel.
So show me the all-in comparison with a reasonable transportation assumption. Don’t include meals because breakfast isn’t equivalent and we’d eat either way.

Using the midpoint of the ride estimates and no rental car:

Hyatt House: $1,454.64 hotel + $68 airport rides + $0 routine local transportation = $1,522.64.

Cambria Riverview: $925.68 hotel + $61 airport rides + $155 for four downtown round trips = $1,141.68.

Cambria remains about $380.96 cheaper. The range is approximately $1,510.64 to $1,534.64 for Hyatt House and $1,095.68 to $1,187.68 for Cambria, before ride tips or surge pricing. Even at the high end for rides, Cambria saves about $323.
That’s a real difference. Is there any catch in the Cambria room wording? Sometimes two queens appears in search and changes when you put in the child.

I rechecked it with two adults and one child age 12 entered. The displayed room remains the two-queen room, occupancy up to four, at the quoted flexible rate. There is no extra-person charge shown for Owen and no rollaway is needed. The total remains $925.68. The rate requires a card guarantee but no advance deposit; payment is collected by the hotel. The only variable not included is breakfast or incidental spending.
Do the same verification on Hyatt House. A full-size sofa bed is fine, but I want it stated in the room details.

Verified with all three travelers entered: the king studio suite is listed for up to four guests and its room details explicitly identify one king bed plus one full-size sofa bed. The $1,454.64 total does not change when Owen is included. No rollaway is required. The flexible rate is guaranteed by card, with no prepayment shown, and the March 25 cancellation deadline remains in effect.
Are those really the best two? I don’t want a bargain across the river if there’s a downtown room only $100 more.

I checked the closest comparable downtown alternatives that accept three guests. The best lower downtown total I found was $1,603.20 for a two-queen room, and its parking was also paid. Another upper-district option was $1,498.76 but used a king plus sofa bed and had a stricter March 24 cancellation deadline. Neither improves materially on Hyatt House.

Across the river, one hotel came in at $861.40, but the available room was a single king and the listing capped occupancy at two. I excluded it rather than assuming Owen could be added. Cambria is the strongest lower-cost result with an unambiguous two-queen setup for three.
Keep both Hyatt House and Cambria available for the flight-and-hotel decision. Don’t reserve either. Summarize the real tradeoff and update the trip total using the flights we already have.

No hotel has been reserved. Both candidates remain in play for March 27-31.

Hyatt House Charleston/Historic District is $1,454.64 for a king studio suite with a full-size sofa bed, verified for three. With estimated airport rides, the lodging and local-transport total is $1,510.64-$1,534.64. It avoids routine downtown rides, although waterfront sights are a longer walk or DASH trip. Cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. March 25. Valet is $49 nightly plus tax, but irrelevant without a rental car.

Cambria Hotel Charleston Riverview is $925.68 for two queens, verified for three, with free parking. Airport and four daily downtown round trips put it at $1,095.68-$1,187.68 before tips. The likely savings are $323-$439, at the cost of roughly 20-50 minutes of daily ride time and less flexibility for midday returns. The bus would take about 40-55 minutes each way and is not a practical primary plan. Cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. March 26.

Adding the $1,068 nonstop flights for three and about $90 for O’Hare parking, the current trip estimate is $2,668.64-$2,692.64 with Hyatt House or $2,253.68-$2,345.68 with Cambria. Both figures exclude meals, ride tips, and optional activities.
